name: Tobias Kloss
current_role: Co-founder, Quantum Systems (Gilching, Germany) — current title not confirmed
profile: One of four co-founders of German drone maker Quantum Systems, incorporated in January 2015 with Florian Seibel, Michael Kriegel and Armin Busse after the Seibel/Kriegel drone work at the Bundeswehr University Munich. Quantum Systems makes eVTOL reconnaissance drones (Trinity, Vector) and AI software, has 1,000+ employees and sites in Germany, Ukraine, the US and Australia.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 Quantum Systems was contracted to supply 15,000 'Strila' interceptor drones to Ukraine's National Guard.
deep_cut_fact: Kloss was among the early collaborators who joined Seibel and Kriegel's Bundeswehr-University drone project before the four of them incorporated Quantum Systems in January 2015; the company's first product was the 'Tron' eVTOL with a 2 kg payload, discontinued in 2020.
notes: Very low public profile. Quantum Systems site blocked by Cloudflare for automated reading; get press contact from its press page. Web-search budget ran out during this lane; research limited to directly fetched pages.

name: Zhang Zhiyuan
current_role: Co-founder, Sironax (维泰瑞隆) — not listed among current corporate leaders or board
profile: Dr. Zhiyuan Zhang co-founded Sironax in 2017 with Dr. Xiaodong Wang (founding director of Beijing's NIBS and BeiGene co-founder). Sironax develops therapies for neurodegenerative, inflammatory and metabolic disease (SARM1 inhibitor SIR2501, NAMPT activator SIR4156, RIPK1 inhibitor SIR9900), has 170+ staff across the US, China, Switzerland and Australia, and is now led by CEO Shefali Agarwal.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Sironax was named to Fierce Biotech's 'Fierce 15', won FDA Fast Track for SIR2501 in chemotherapy-induced neuropathy, and Novartis exercised its option to acquire Sironax's brain-delivery platform.
deep_cut_fact: Sironax started as a Cayman-registered company in 2017, set up its Beijing R&D centre in 2018 and ran its first clinical operations in Australia in 2019 before moving its HQ to the US (Waltham) in 2025.
notes: Hurun industry tag may not reflect biotech. His current role is unclear (not on the leadership or board pages). Web-search budget ran out, so his personal background was not researched further.

name: Mike Smayda
current_role: Co-founder of Hermeus (formerly Chief Product Officer); current role unclear
profile: Dr. Michael Smayda is one of four Generation Orbit engineers (USAF X-60A hypersonic program) who founded Hermeus in Atlanta in Nov 2018 with AJ Piplica, Glenn Case and Skyler Shuford, and served as its Chief Product Officer. Hermeus builds uncrewed supersonic Quarterhorse aircraft for defense, hit unicorn status in April 2026 and reached supersonic flight 364 days after its first flight.
interesting_fact: Hermeus says it is the fastest company in aviation history to go from founding to supersonic flight, and built the world's first private unmanned supersonic jet.
deep_cut_fact: He and his co-founders learned startup-building at Generation Orbit under former Georgia Tech professor John Olds, then made a few hundred cold calls to investors from kitchen tables and coffee shops, with no office until May 2019.
notes: Not on Hermeus's current leadership page; his former bio page (hermeus.com/mike-smayda) is offline, so his current role is unclear. Low public profile.
